{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My roommate claims he 'just doesn't know how' to clean the bathroom properly. He's an engineer who designs precision instruments. He's learned that if he does a bad enough job, I'll eventually just do it myself. Strategic incompetence.

CANDIDATE A:
A committee member claimed he could never understand the grant-submission system. Every time he entered the budget incorrectly, I repaired and submitted it for him. Months later I learned he used the same system perfectly for his private consulting work. He had discovered that repeated mistakes made his administrative responsibilities become mine.

CANDIDATE B:
My roommate truly doesn't know how to clean the bathroom properly. He's a software developer, brilliant with code but helpless with household tasks. No matter how many times I showed him, he kept using dish soap on the tiles and leaving streaks everywhere. It's not strategic—he genuinely struggles with cleaning and eventually we split chores so he handles things he's good at instead.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:9"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve individuals feigning incompetence to shift responsibilities onto someone else."}
